sector: Steel (MS billets, TMT bars, structural steel), with ship recycling, scrap trading and real estate
headline: PAT rose from Rs 61.4 m to Rs 823.8 m and EBITDA margin from 5.9% to 18.6% over FY24-FY26, but manufactured-goods revenue grew only 4.7% in FY26 (the rest is scrap and raw-material sales), group entities are about a quarter of sales and over a third of purchases, and the Rs 90 reference is 32x FY26 EPS against a steel-peer median of 13.9x, so the RHP price band and an explanation of FY26's margin decide the case.
red_flags: PAT Rs 61.4 m / 437.5 m / 823.8 m FY24-FY26; EBITDA margin 5.9% / 10.2% / 18.6%; ROE 21.0% on book equity; Reg 6(1) average operating profit Rs 576.6 m (pp. 179, 410, 571)

FY26 revenue +30.4%, but manufactured goods +4.7% (TMT volume -1.8%, realisation -4.0%); other operating income +Rs 1,654.3 m, mostly non-ferrous scrap Rs 1,520.6 m with no disclosed margin (pp. 290, 529)

Capacity build ahead of revenue: Rolling Mill 2 at 5.5% use, Rolling Mill 3 due 31-Dec-2026, Rs 4,043 m power plant, Rs 2,244 m melting shop; borrowings Rs 3,575.7 m to Rs 5,024.1 m by 30-Jun-2026 (pp. 50, 152, 299)
Group trading: related-party sales 23.1% of revenue (59.1% in FY25), purchases 35.7%, guarantees Rs 782.3 m; five of the top-10 customers (49.0% of revenue) are or were related (pp. 31, 38, 48)
Cash: CFO Rs -165.5 / -276.8 / +825.3 m (29.0% of cumulative PAT); FY26 includes a Rs 1,182 m inventory release, Rs 1,190 m of advances inside CFO and Rs 249.3 m unpaid tax (pp. 107, 440, 447)

Three statutory-audit changes in FY26 and three CFOs since Oct-2024; Rs 844.1 m FY21 transactions of a merged company noted by the tax department; Rs 90 reference = 32.1x FY26 EPS vs peer P/E 11.1x-27.2x (pp. 117, 177-178, 386, 543)
reference_note: Rs 90 = the issue price of the five cash private placements of 17-Dec-2025 to 23-Mar-2026 (Rs 2 shares), the DRHP's weighted average cost of its latest primary issues (pp. 186-189). It is a reference to size the model, not a price band and not a view of the right price. Secondary transfers in the same window were at Rs 15 to Rs 30 and 19.46 m shares moved by gift at nil; the Sep-Dec 2024 rounds were at Rs 30 per Rs 2 share (p. 443).

flags: AMBER: DCF and relative diverge by -90.1% - the divergence is the finding; name its cause
DEGENERATE: TV above 100% of EV - fix assumptions, do not report
model.reverse_dcf: Current free cash flow is negative, so no multiple can be stated: the price assumes cash generation improves from here.
